facts.statement: Ignavusaurus fossils were found in the Upper Elliot Formation, dating to approximately 200 million years ago during the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Upper Elliot Formation which is probably Hettangian in age around 200 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus was described based on a partial but well-preserved articulated skeleton.
facts.quote: It was described on the basis of a partial, well preserved articulated skeleton.

facts.statement: The type species Ignavusaurus rachelis was formally described in 2010 by the Spanish paleontologist F. Knoll.
facts.quote: The type species, Ignavusaurus rachelis, was described in 2010 by Spanish palaeontologist F. Knoll.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in southern Lesotho near the locality known as Ha Ralekoala.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in southern Lesotho near Ha Ralekoala.

facts.statement: The fossils were found mostly articulated, but the skull was badly damaged and broken into more than 120 fragments.
facts.quote: The fossils were discovered in a mostly articulated state, although the skull was badly damaged, having broken into more than 120 fragments.

facts.statement: The remains were mentioned in an unpublished 2002 doctoral dissertation but remained formally undescribed for several years.
facts.quote: An unpublished 2002 Ph. dissertation referred to the remains, but they were not formally described for several years, and the find remained unpublished.

facts.statement: The fossils were temporarily catalogued as BM HR 20 at the National Museum of Natural History in Paris.
facts.quote: The fossils were brought to the National Museum of Natural History in Paris, where they were provisionally catalogued as BM HR 20

facts.statement: The holotype individual measured about 1.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 22.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype had a body length of about 1.5 m and weighed about 22.5 kg.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of the humerus and femur suggests the holotype was a fast-growing individual, possibly less than one year old.
facts.quote: Histological analysis of the humerus and femur indicates that BM HR 20 was fast-growing individual, maybe less than one year old, based on age determination studies.

facts.statement: Ignavusaurus possessed a long, slender neck and tail, similar to other early sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Like other early sauropodomorphs, Ignavusaurus had a long, slender neck and tail.

facts.statement: Ignavusaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph, a type of long-necked, herbivorous saurischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Ignavusaurus is a basal sauropodomorph, a member of the long-necked, herbivorous, saurischian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Ignavusaurus might be synonymous with Massospondylus, arguing that its primitive features are actually juvenile traits.
facts.quote: Yates et al. (2011) noted that some characters used to place Ignavusaurus outside Massopoda are reflective of juvenile status and instead are more similar to juvenile Massospondylus, considering Ignavusaurus probably synonymous with Massospondylus.

facts.statement: Other cladistic analyses have found Ignavusaurus to be a valid genus most closely related to Sarahsaurus within the group Massopoda.
facts.quote: Meanwhile, a cladistic analysis presented by Apaldetti et al. (2011) found Ignavusaurus to be a valid genus which is most closely related to Sarahsaurus within Massopoda

facts.statement: Ignavusaurus is placed within the family Massospondylidae.
Ignavusaurus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Ignavusaurus was an extinct basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now Lesotho.
rejected.quote: Ignavusaurus is an extinct monospecific genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now Lesotho.
